title: Memory Limits
summary: AI forgets — the app must remember what matters.

sections.heading: Orientation
sections.subtitle: Orientation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What will you understand? Why does AI 'forget'? — And how to design your product to remember what needs to be remembered.
- Why now? A long conversation = context fills up. Without design — the assistant seems to be 'talking to a wall'.
- What after the lesson? You will identify 3 things the app should always remember.

sections.heading: Tension
sections.subtitle: You agreed — and after 10 messages, it forgot
sections.contentMarkdown:
- You explained an idea, you agreed on a plan — and soon the AI started suggesting the opposite of what you said.
- It's not you — the AI really forgets. This is not a personal flaw — it's a design limitation.
- When building an AI feature — don't expect that the 'conversation' will remember everything — the app needs to remember what is important.

sections.heading: Core idea
sections.subtitle: AI does not remember forever
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Context Window = the amount of text the AI can see in the conversation — not a permanent archive.
- Signs you've gone beyond the window: it repeats itself, forgets your name, contradicts decisions, makes up details.
- The solution in the product: the app remembers 3-5 fixed facts (name, preferences, decisions) and passes them with every request.
- In conversation: a short summary every 15-20 messages — 'Status summary: 1)... 2)...'.

sections.heading: Comparison
sections.subtitle: Talking and waiting vs summarizing and passing
sections.contentMarkdown:
| 'Continue from the beginning' | Summary + passing from the app |
|----------------|---------------------------|
| 30-message conversation — 'Continue from what I told you.' It forgot. It will start guessing — and you will build on incorrect information | 'Summary: 1) project... 2) decisions... 3) open...' + the app passes the username and preferences every time |

sections.heading: Glossary
sections.subtitle: Two terms to start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|---------|--------|------|
| Context Window | The maximum amount of text the AI sees in the conversation — not a permanent archive | After 50 messages — the first message was deleted from its temporary memory |
| State Snapshot | A short summary of the current state — to give back to the AI when the conversation gets long | 'We decided: blue color, young audience, open: pricing page.' |

sections.heading: Screenshot block (intent)
sections.contentMarkdown: Limited memory — explicit design: The alert is not legal — it is an acknowledgment that memory has limits. The assistant sees your context + part of the content — not 'everything'. In your product: define what the app saves outside the conversation and passes it every time.

sections.heading: Quiz
sections.subtitle: Quick confirmation
sections.contentMarkdown:
Question: After a week of conversation — the AI forgot your name and contradicted a decision you agreed on. What is the closest reason?
You went outside the Context Window — the information fell out of the window.
The AI had a sudden hallucination unrelated to memory.
The problem is in your tone.
Explanation: When it forgets basics — often the information is not in the window. The solution: the app saves and passes.

sections.heading: Mission
sections.subtitle: 3 things the app should remember
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: Imagine an app with an AI assistant — identify 3 facts the app should remember (not that the AI remembers on its own). 10-15 minutes. Delivery: 1. Type of app (e.g., store, education, booking)
2. 3 things it should always remember — for each one: - What is the fact? - Why is it important if forgotten? - How does the app pass it? (database field, session, at the start of each prompt)
3. State Snapshot sentence if the conversation gets long. Evaluation criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| 3 practical facts | 60% | Each fact has a reason 'if forgotten'; the passing method is realistic |
| Snapshot | 40% | The summary is short and focused; covers current decisions or state |

- You can: identify 3 facts + Snapshot for any conversation feature.
